interest: This file offers valuable insight into the rigid commercial controls enforced during the early Allied occupation of Japan under SCAP, demonstrating how long-standing pre-war commercial channels—such as transatlantic horticultural ties between American nurseries and prominent Japanese exporters like the Yokohama Nursery Company—were suspended in favor of state monopolies like the U.S. Commercial Company. Furthermore, the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture's formal petition for Japanese rice seed samples illustrates the early post-war resumption of international agronomic networks and the global scientific demand for Japanese agricultural genetics despite military occupation and strict diplomatic clearance protocols.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.613, 'Agriculture., Japan, Field Crops. Seeds.') documents inquiries and regulatory procedures concerning the export and acquisition of seeds from occupied Japan between May 1946 and June 1947. The records consist of correspondence involving an American commercial nurseryman seeking to resume pre-war seed imports from the Yokohama Nursery Co., Ltd., the State Department's clarification of the ban on private trade and referral to the U.S. Commercial Company under the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), and a diplomatic despatch cover sheet from the American Embassy in Cairo transmitting an official request by the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture for samples of Japanese rice seed.

subfiles.about: The Department of State explains restrictions barring private trade with occupied Japan and advises an American nurseryman to submit seed import requests through the U.S. Commercial Company.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Acting Chief, Japanese and Korean Affairs Division, Department of State
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Roswell H. Whitman replies to Allen J. Hankele's inquiry regarding the purchase of horticultural seeds from the Yokohama Nursery Co., Ltd. He explains that private commercial trade between Japanese entities and foreign firms is prohibited under the occupation regime and that all exports are administered through government bodies. For U.S. imports, the U.S. Commercial Company handles transactions and can liaise with General MacArthur's headquarters in Japan to determine seed availability.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Allen J. Hankel regarding seed procurement from Japan
subfiles.to: Allen J. Hankel, Proprietor, Alanwold Nursery

subfiles.about: An American nurseryman requests guidance from the Department of State on how to send a commercial order for seeds to the Yokohama Nursery Company in post-war Japan.
subfiles.from: Allen J. Hankele, Proprietor, Alanwold Nursery
subfiles.summary: Allen J. Hankele of Alanwold Nursery in Neshaminy, Pennsylvania, writes to the U.S. State Department explaining that his business operations are severely hampered by the absence of Japanese seed supplies. He asks if there is any permissible channel through which he can place an order with the Yokohama Nursery Co., Ltd. Hankele stresses that orders need to be dispatched quickly so that the nursery in Yokohama can gather seeds in season.
subfiles.title: Letter from Allen J. Hankele to U.S. State Department requesting procedure to order Japanese seeds

subfiles.about: The American Embassy in Cairo transmits an official request by the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture for Japanese rice seed samples.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Cairo, Egypt (drafted by R. B. Elwood)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 2670 from the American Embassy in Cairo, drafted by R. B. Elwood, transmits a formal application from the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture seeking samples of rice seed from Japan. The document records receipt by the Department of State in July 1947 and internal distribution across regional and economic divisions, including Near Eastern Affairs and Far Eastern Affairs. It is cross-referenced with related State Department decimal files on Egyptian agriculture and grains.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2670 from American Embassy Cairo on Egyptian request for Japanese rice seed samples
